title: PUBLIC SERVICE COUNTER HOURS OF OPERATION CHANGE
content:
For almost the last decade, the PMPD was able to offer expanded hours with the Public Safety Building open past 4 PM to 7 PM Monday to Friday.  As the PMPD continues to optimize internal processes, the PMPD made the difficult decision to shift resourcing into other areas of the organization to better support operations and improve public safety.  The emergency telephone just outside the main front doors of the Public Safety Building remains available to the public 24/7.  The PMPD has seen significant improvements in the ability of EComm to provide reduced wait times for non-emergency calls and emergency calls remain well within target answer times.
Chief Constable Fleugel noted, “coupled with the improvements at EComm, we have successfully implemented online crime reporting and transitioned to an online Police Information Check system several years ago with good success.  We are just not seeing the foot traffic at to the police office in the evening hours to justify the use of precious salary dollars at those hours any longer.  Our core business hours remain unchanged.”

title: Port Moody Police phase in body-worn cameras
content:
-These cameras are mounted to officers’ uniforms and will record interactions for evidentiary and accountability purposes.
-Officers will activate their cameras as soon as practical during interactions with the public and will also inform the person being recorded as soon as practical.
-Officers will not continuously record on their cameras if they are not responding to a specific incident. There may be times when officers will use discretion not to record interactions that are sensitive in nature including in healthcare settings, places of worship and in courtrooms.
“The introduction of body-worn cameras is an important milestone for our department and our community. These cameras provide an impartial record of interactions, enhance transparency and accountability and help strengthen public trust. The PMPD consulted the community for our 2024-2026 Strategic Plan and learned that citizens were supportive of introducing this technology and we are now ready to do that. Body-worn cameras will support our officers by capturing critical evidence and providing greater clarity during complex incidents. Ultimately, body-worn cameras are another tool that helps us deliver professional, modern, and effective policing to the citizens of Port Moody." – Chief Constable David Fleugel.
The Port Moody Police Department anticipates a full rollout of body-worn cameras to frontline officers by late 2026.

title: THREE SUSPECTS CAUGHT CLIMBING TOWER CRANE
content:
A trio of teenage boys were arrested Thursday evening after allegedly climbing a tower crane.
On May 7, 2026 just before 11 p.m., frontline officers were called to a fully fenced construction site in the 2300 block of St Johns Street for a report of trespassers who were actively climbing a tower crane.
Officers arrived within several minutes and observed the suspects who had ascended the crane. The trio surrendered and were arrested without incident – later released to guardians as investigators consider charge recommendation.
“It should go without saying, these stunts are not only illegal but dangerous,” states Constable Sam Zacharias, adding that “construction sites like this one are live monitored around-the-clock with video and motion sensors – police will always be called in instances of trespassers.”

title: WANTED MAN ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGED CRIME SPREE
content:
An alert citizen helped Port Moody Police capture a wanted man after an alleged property crime spree.
On April 26, 2026, around 9:45 p.m., Port Moody Police officers were called to a report of a possible theft in the Ioco Road corridor of Port Moody. The caller reported seeing a man rummaging through multiple vehicles in the residential neighbourhood. Officers patrolled the area and were not able to locate the suspect initially, however, did obtain surveillance footage of the incident. Approximately an hour later, the man was located by officers several kilometers away and arrested without incident. Of note, the man was also wanted on an outstanding arrest warrant.
The
B.C. Prosecution Service
has approved two counts of mischief and five counts of breaching a release order against 31-year-old Marc Smaaslet. Smaaslet remains in custody at this time and has his next court appearance later this morning.
“Incidents like these are a great reminder of the vital role the public plays in helping us curb crime in our community,” states Constable Sam Zacharias. “We thank the diligent witness who contacted us right away and helped advance our investigation – leading to the eventual arrest of the accused.”

title: DRIVER FLEES, CRASHES WITH PASSENGER IN TRUNK
content:
Port Moody Police investigated an unusual collision Saturday morning.
On April 18, 2026 just after 4 a.m., a patrol officer spotted a heavily occupied Honda sedan with an ‘N’ decal travelling on Clarke Road. The officer turned his police vehicle around to attempt to stop the vehicle and the driver of the Honda fled onto a side street. A short time later, the officer located the vehicle which had crashed into the front yard of a residential home.
In addition to the driver, 5 passengers were located inside of the vehicle. One passenger was inside of the vehicle’s trunk at the time of the collision.
The 19-year-old class 7 driver did not pass the roadside alcohol screening test and now faces multiple Motor Vehicle Act charges and a driving prohibition. All of the parties were assessed by firefighters at scene.
“Fortunately, there were no serious injuries reported as a result of this collision,” states Constable Sam Zacharias, adding that “this vehicle had more occupants than seats and it certainly could have been a far worse outcome. We would like to remind the public to always plan a safe ride home – there are so many options available including public transit and rideshares.”

title: UNSAFE TRUCK PULLED FROM ROADWAY
content:
Port Moody Police officers observed a startling incident Wednesday morning when a commercial vehicle lost two wheels while travelling on the highway.
On March 11, 2026 around 10:30 a.m., frontline officers were travelling near a dump truck entering Port Moody on westbound Barnet Highway. Officers observed the dump truck’s two rear wheels and a brake drum become dislodged – hurling into other lanes of traffic. Officers were able to safely avoid the objects but one of the wheels did strike a bystander’s vehicle causing damage. It was determined the lug nuts were not properly fastened and the vehicle was removed from the road for a complete inspection. The driver was also issued a violation ticket by officers.
“We routinely conduct commercial vehicle enforcement in Port Moody and incidents like these reinforce the importance of this type of enforcement,” states Constable Sam Zacharias, adding that “this could have been much worse and it is fortunate there were no injuries as a result.”

title: PORT MOODY POLICE BOARD ADVISES OF CHIEF CONSTABLE’S RETIREMENT
content:
The Port Moody Police Board announces that Chief Constable David Fleugel has formally notified the Board of his decision to retire from the Port Moody Police Department at the end of 2026, concluding a distinguished policing career of more than thirty years.
Chief Constable Fleugel joined the Port Moody Police Department in 2017 and has provided steady, principled leadership during a time of significant change in policing. His tenure has been marked by a strong commitment to community safety, organizational excellence, and collaborative partnerships.
Under his leadership, Port Moody has remained one of the safest communities in British Columbia, reflecting his focus on community-based policing, crime prevention, and public trust. Chief Constable Fleugel also successfully guided the department through the COVID-19 pandemic and the evolving complexities of modern policing.
Mayor Meghan Lahti, Police Board Chair expressed her appreciation: “On behalf of the Port Moody Police Board and the community we serve, I want to extend our sincere appreciation to Chief Constable Fleugel for his outstanding leadership and service. Since joining PMPD in 2017, he has demonstrated unwavering dedication to public safety and has guided the department with professionalism and integrity.”
Chief Constable Fleugel has indicated his intention to remain in his role through the end of 2026 to support a thoughtful leadership transition, though timelines may be adjusted as needed to
ensure continuity.
The Police Board will begin a recruitment process to identify the next Chief Constable. Further details about the transition will be shared in the coming months.

title: POLICE INVESTIGATE TWO SERIOUS COLLISIONS
content:
FILE:
2026-2919 / 2922
Port Moody Police are investigating two back-to-back serious collisions Tuesday evening.
On June 23, 2026 at about 7:15 p.m., the Port Moody Police Department and other first responders were called to the 600 block of Ioco Road for a report of a 3-vehicle collision. It is believed the driver of a pick-up truck travelled into the oncoming lane and struck two vehicles. The pick-up truck ended up off the road into a utility pole.
The driver of the pick-up truck – a 41-year-old man – was detained after allegedly failing a roadside alcohol screening test and faces criminal charges as a result. He was driving with a young child in the rear seat and also determined to be a province-wide prohibited driver. Fortunately, there were no serious injuries reported but the road was closed into the early hours of Wednesday morning as crews worked to restore the utility pole [see photos of collision].
Approximately an hour after the first collision, officers and first responders were called to a report of a hit & run on St Johns Street at Ioco Road. A cyclist was allegedly struck by a white BMW SUV of which the driver did not remain on scene. The cyclist suffered serious but non-life-threatening injuries as a result. “This matter remains under investigation and we are appealing for any additional witnesses or anyone with dash camera footage to contact us,” states Constable Sam Zacharias.

title: COMMUNITY SAFETY TRAILER TO BE DEPLOYED IN PORT MOODY
content:
The Port Moody Police Department has acquired a Community Safety Trailer thanks to provincial funding. The trailer will be deployed in the near future and here are some important takeaways for the public:
The trailer is equipped with secure video cameras that passively record video.
The purpose of the trailer is to be strategically deployed in various areas of Port Moody to deter criminal activity and, if necessary, provide video evidence to aid an investigation.
The video captured is only retained in the event it may aid an investigation.
The trailer is clearly marked and will be positioned in public places.
The trailer is powered by solar panels and it does not require an additional power source.
A privacy impact assessment has been conducted and the trailer will be deployed in accordance with applicable privacy legislation.
“We believe this is another tool that will help us deter and solve crime in our city,” states Inspector Brad Sheridan, adding that “though this is new for our community, we know many other local communities have had success with the addition of Community Safety Trailers.”
This project has been funded by the Province’s Community Safety & Targeted Enforcement Program (or C-STEP) and we are grateful for their contribution.

title: POLICE KEPT BUSY AT SASAMAT LAKE YESTERDAY EVENING
content:
Port Moody Police were kept busy attending calls for service at Sasamat Lake on Friday evening.
On July 24, 2026 just before 7:30 p.m., officers were called to the lake’s float walk for a fight involving numerous individuals. A bystander jumped in an attempt to stop the melee and unfortunately sustained injuries – including the loss of several of his teeth. The suspects dispersed prior to police arrival and investigators would like to speak with any additional witnesses.
Police were also kept busy at the lake throughout the evening with other calls including the arrest of a very intoxicated female in a trail – who at one point had to be carried by officers. Frontline officers fielded a report of a male who went missing while out for a swim, but fortunately was later located safely. As well, much later in the evening, officers assisted security guards with ejecting several trespassers who were refusing to leave the lake hours past its closing time.
“This lake becomes quite busy in the summer months and we tend to see an uptick in calls for service,” states Constable Sam Zacharias. “We want to once again reiterate that there is no tolerance for consumption of drugs or alcohol at this park. We work closely with park rangers to ensure it is a safe environment for all parkgoers and we encourage anyone who witnesses unruly or unsafe behaviour to contact us right away.”

title: EV CHARGING CABLES CUT AT REC COMPLEX
content:
Port Moody Police are investigating after multiple EV fast-chargers were damaged early Tuesday morning.
On July 28, 2026 at around 1 a.m., officers were called to the Port Moody Recreation Complex on Ioco Road by security who reported numerous EV charging cables had been cut after sensors alerted them to the damage. Officers attended the scene and noted 6 of the cables had been cut and subsequently stolen, rendering the fast-chargers inoperable.
“We are in the evidence gathering phase of this investigation which includes canvassing for possible CCTV footage,” states Constable Sam Zacharias, adding that “the chargers are currently out of commission as BC Hydro works to repair them.”
Any potential witnesses or anyone who has information on this incident is asked to contact the Port Moody Police Department.

title: Charge approved in dog bite incident
content:
A criminal charge has been approved against the owner of two dogs after the dogs allegedly mauled a woman.
On May 20, 2026, Port Moody Police frontline officers along with other first responders were called to the Moody Centre area of Port Moody for reports of a woman who had sustained serious injuries after two large dogs attacked her. The woman was transported to hospital by paramedics.
Officers spoke with over a dozen witnesses and compiled other material evidence, later sending a report to Crown Counsel. The B.C. Prosecution Service has now approved a charge of criminal negligence causing bodily harm against Jessica Rex.
“It is alleged that these dogs had previously been deemed aggressive by City officials, but were not wearing required muzzles at the time of the incident,” states Constable Sam Zacharias. “The victim sustained serious, life-altering injuries as a result of the mauling and continues to recover from the attack. We thank those who remained on scene and rendered first aid until medical personnel arrived.”

title: Alleged sexual exploitation case results in charges
content:
FILE
: 2025-2476
Charges have been approved stemming from a child exploitation investigation.
The Port Moody Police Department received information in the Spring of 2025, alleging a vulnerable youth had been sexually exploited by an adult male within the Lower Mainland.
Officers launched an investigation which ultimately led to the arrest of a 58-year-old North Vancouver man, Majid Talebi. On August 11, 2026, the B.C. Prosecution Service approved the following charges against Talebi: one count of invitation to sexual touching of a person under 16 years and two counts of telecommunication to lure a child under 16 years.
“This was a very complex and sensitive investigation carried out by our Major Crime Section which included a tandem civil forfeiture process,” states Constable Sam Zacharias, adding that “Detectives worked diligently over the past year to collect evidence and bring this matter before the courts.”
Talebi is due in Port Coquitlam Provincial Court for his first appearance this morning. The Court has ordered a publication ban prohibiting the publication of any information that could identify the victim.
